prisoner.name: Jamie Bauer
prisoner.description: Jamie Bauer is a New York activist and direct-action trainer involved in Women's Pentagon Action and ACT UP. They were among the Waterloo 54 arrested during a 1983 peace walk to the Seneca encampment and spent several days confined in a school cafeteria before release.

cases.charges: Arrest during the Waterloo peace walk; exact filed charge unverified
cases.sentence: Held for several days after the July 30, 1983 peace walk. Bauer recalled approximately four or five days before release on recognizance as a Jane Doe. Confinement was in a junior high school cafeteria. Exact release date and any judicial sentence remain unverified.

entries.custody_evidence: Bauer personally describes several days of confinement, followed by recognizance release, in the recorded 2004 interview.
entries.research_notes: The contemporary collective statement establishes July 30. Its threatened incitement charge is not treated as the filed charge. No release date or exact duration is calculated. Birthdate remains unknown; archival coverage dates and ages are not birthdate evidence. Coordinates approximate Waterloo, the arrest locality, not a detention facility. Historical name is a duplicate-check key only; display name and pronouns follow the later interview.
